title: Onboarding / Governance intake — Merrick Capital
next_steps: Priya to circulate redline copy of MSA/DPA by 2025-09-05
Ben to upload network diagram and SOC2 summary link to CRM by 2025-09-02
Provide Dedicated pricing worksheet and committed capacity options by 2025-09-03
Schedule private deployment technical deep-dive w/ infra team for week of 2025-09-08
action_items: Priya Nair: Send MSA + DPA redlines (2025-09-05)
Ben Li: Share SOC2 summary + network diagram (2025-09-02)
Sam Patel: Confirm internal procurement timeline & PO approver list (2025-09-04)
Jordan Wu: Provide list of expected throughput/latency SLOs for pilot (2025-09-03)
summary: Intro call to intake governance and procurement requirements for a pilot. Customer walked through legal redlines (DPA/MSA) and procurement gating items: SOC2, network diagram, SLA thresholds, and pricing approval flow. Redwood AE/SE committed to sharing redlines, SOC2 artifacts and a dedicated pricing worksheet; technical deep-dive requested for private/Dedicated options. Next steps and owners assigned.
transcript: 00:00:02 - Priya Nair: Hi everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Priya, AE on the account, and with me is Ben, our solutions engineer. How's it going?
00:00:09 - Jordan Wu: Hey, thanks. Doing well. Appreciate you making time. We wanted to get aligned on procurement gating and the legal stack before a pilot request goes to our budget committee.
00:00:21 - Leah Morales: Hi all, Leah from legal. I have our redlines to the DPA and a few vendor governance questions — mostly around data residency and breach notification timelines.

00:00:33 - Ben Li: Thanks Leah. We have an internal MSA + DPA template we can share, and Redwood supports both hosted and private deployments with different controls. We'll walk through what maps to which option.

00:00:47 - Sam Patel: Quick ask from procurement — we need a clear SLA and pricing boundary for pilot vs production. Also the procurement workflow is: PO approvals require legal signoff then finance signoff. So the faster we get the MSA in a near-final state, the quicker we can move.
00:01:05 - Priya Nair: Understood. For clarity, is the pilot expected to use hosted Redwood API or do you anticipate needing a VPC/private deployment from day one?

00:01:13 - Jordan Wu: Likely hosted for initial eval but with a hard requirement that data not leave our EU region, and if metrics pass we'll request a dedicated or private deployment. We need to map those transitions in the contract.
00:01:26 - Leah Morales: Right, for EU data residency we need contract language and confirmation of cloud regions and subprocessors. Also, breach notification in 72 hours is non-negotiable for us.

00:01:38 - Ben Li: Okay. Our standard DPA supports subprocessor disclosures and we can provide a redacted subprocessors list. Regarding region, we have EU-hosted endpoints — I'll flag which models and regions are available. 72-hour notification is something we can discuss with Security team — it's broadly in our practices but I'll confirm exact wording.
00:01:58 - Sam Patel: Another practical point — we do a vendor security gate where SOC2 Type II and penetration test summaries are required. Do you have those readily available?
00:02:07 - Priya Nair: Yes; we can share SOC2 summary and a network architecture diagram. Ben, do we have a short pen test statement?

00:02:14 - Ben Li: We have a pen-test summary and controls map we can share after a quick redaction. I'll put those in the CRM link. I'll also include a one-page digest on encryption at rest/in transit and KMS integrations.

00:02:27 - Jordan Wu: Great. On pricing, conceptually we want two numbers: pilot variable pricing and a committed capacity price. Procurement will need the committed discount bands and the minimum term. Is that standard?

00:02:38 - Priya Nair: Yes, we offer usage-based for hosted plus reserved/dedicated with monthly commits for Dedicated. We'll send a pricing worksheet that shows per-token for pilot and reserved tiers for production with examples. We can also show cost per 1M tokens under a 12-month commit.

00:02:55 - Leah Morales: One redline item in the MSA: indemnity carve-outs and limitation of liability — we may ask for clarification on data breaches tied to vendor negligence vs customer prompt. We'll send the clauses we prefer.

00:03:06 - Priya Nair: That's fine; please send the exact language and we'll review. In past enterprise deals we've had a negotiation on liability caps tied to subscription fees; we can flag that for legal.
00:03:16 - Sam Patel: Timeline wise, procurement wants a decision by mid-September for a Q4 pilot kick-off. We need final pricing and redlined MSA in hand by the first week of September ideally.

00:03:26 - Priya Nair: Noted — we'll aim to deliver redlines and the pricing worksheet in that window. Ben, can you prepare a tech packet for Jordan with expected latencies and throughput per model variant?

00:03:33 - Ben Li: Yup, I'll produce a packet with performance baselines, expected p95 latency numbers for the hosted and dedicated options, and notes around batching and KV-cache impacts. Also include a note about cold start behavior.
00:03:46 - Jordan Wu: On the technical side — our ops team will want to run a throughput test. If we pilot on hosted, what's the path to run a bench with our prompt sets?

00:03:54 - Ben Li: We can run a benchmark: you can share a prompt corpus, we run it against shortlisted models and capture latency/cost numbers. For private/Dedicated we can run the same workload in a dedicated capacity and compare. I'll document test-plan steps.
00:04:09 - Leah Morales: Also please confirm audit logging: we need immutable audit logs accessible for 12 months and API-level access logs for investigations. Can Redwood provide that on hosted?

00:04:19 - Priya Nair: Hosted provides request logs and usage analytics; for longer retention and immutable logs we typically recommend Dedicated or Private where retention policies can be tuned. We'll document options and tradeoffs.

00:04:31 - Sam Patel: Worth noting our procurement has a vendor gating checklist — items include legal signoff, SOC2, network diag, SSO/SAML setup, and a data flow diagram. If any one of these is missing, approval stalls.
00:04:42 - Jordan Wu: Regarding SSO, we use Okta and require SAML SSO plus SCIM provisioning for service accounts. Do you support that?

00:04:48 - Ben Li: Yes, Redwood supports SAML and SCIM provisioning for user accounts in the Console for Dedicated/Private customers. For hosted customers we can enable SSO for the Console and provide scoped credentials for API access.
00:05:02 - Leah Morales: Are there any subprocessors or third parties who handle request data for model inference? We need a subprocessors list for procurement record-keeping.
00:05:10 - Priya Nair: We'll provide the subprocessors disclosure. For hosted inference we do rely on cloud providers in those regions; for Dedicated we can isolate to an agreed cloud account or VPC.

00:05:22 - Sam Patel: On the MSA timeline, if we get the redline by Sep 5 and turn it around in a week, procurement can start approvals. But Leah, you may need a couple of days to circulate internally.
00:05:30 - Leah Morales: Yes. I'll circulate once I have a redline copy. One ask — can we get a short legal FAQ mapping common MSA clauses to our preferred language? That speeds internal approvals.

00:05:39 - Priya Nair: We can attach a clause-by-clause cheat sheet. We'll highlight common points: liability cap, data residency, breach notifications, and subprocessors. Ben will add notes on what maps to hosted vs private.
00:05:49 - Jordan Wu: On performance SLOs: we need p95 latency under 250ms for short responses and throughput to sustain 50 concurrent requests at peak. Is that realistic on hosted right away?

00:05:59 - Ben Li: Short answer: depends on model and token lengths. For smaller open models you can be under 250ms p95 at modest concurrency; larger models will be higher. We can run the benchmark against your prompts to validate. For guaranteed SLOs you'd typically pick Dedicated with reserved throughput.
00:06:16 - Priya Nair: If you need an SLA for prod with credits/penalties, that's part of the Dedicated enterprise contract; hosted has best-effort but we do publish performance profiles.
00:06:26 - Sam Patel: Can you summarize what items would push us to Dedicated vs staying hosted for pilot?

00:06:31 - Ben Li: Dedicated recommended if you need firm latency SLOs, higher throughput isolation, longer audit log retention, or strict networking controls (e.g., private peering). If your needs are looser, hosted is faster to start.
00:06:43 - Jordan Wu: One more security point — encryption key control. We need an option to use our KMS for encryption at rest for sensitive artifacts. Is customer-managed KMS supported?

00:06:52 - Priya Nair: Customer-managed KMS is supported for Dedicated and Private. For hosted customers, we encrypt with provider KMS; we can discuss a managed key option depending on the commitment.
00:07:03 - Leah Morales: Great. Also request for compliance — do you have ISO certifications or pending assessments? Procurement will ask for certification evidence.
00:07:10 - Ben Li: We are SOC2 Type II. We're in the process for some ISO scopes — I'll confirm exact status and share what we have in the CRM link.

00:07:18 - Sam Patel: Ok, sounds like the action list. For the pricing worksheet, can you include an example TCO for 3-month pilot at 50 req/s with moderate token sizes? Our finance team wants a modeled estimate.
00:07:28 - Priya Nair: Yes — we'll include a TCO model with assumptions you can edit. We'll show pilot variable pricing and a sample committed discount for 12-month reserved capacity.
00:07:38 - Jordan Wu: For procurement gating, Sam and I will share the official vendor intake form after this call. Leah will add the legal redline notes. Expect that in 24 hours.
00:07:46 - Leah Morales: Yep. I'll aim to send the redline and preferred clause language within 48 hours.
00:07:52 - Ben Li: One operational note — if you plan to push to Dedicated later we can pre-provision capacity in a staging pool to make the switch less disruptive.
00:07:59 - Jordan Wu: That would be helpful. Also is there a standard lead time for Dedicated capacity?
00:08:06 - Ben Li: Typically 2–4 weeks depending on GPU type and capacity; we can accelerate with committed purchase. We'll include expected lead times in the technical packet.
00:08:17 - Sam Patel: Onboarding checklist — can you give a one-pager of procurement artifacts we should attach to our vendor file?
00:08:23 - Priya Nair: We'll provide a procurement-ready packet: MSA/DPA redline, SOC2 summary, network diagram, subprocessors list, SSO/SCIM setup guide, and pricing worksheet.
00:08:32 - Jordan Wu: Excellent. Last question — do you have standard termination assistance clauses (e.g., data export within X days)? We need to ensure continuity if we switch vendors.
00:08:40 - Leah Morales: Yes, please include data return/export timelines in the DPA redlines. We typically ask for 60 days retention for exports.
00:08:48 - Priya Nair: We'll include standard termination assistance language and note export timelines; we can discuss 60 days as a possible term.
00:08:55 - Ben Li: I'll also capture notes on data retention defaults per environment in the tech packet — hosted vs dedicated vs private differences.
00:09:03 - Jordan Wu: Great. That covers most of our targets. If we get the redline and pricing by early September procurement can slot us into the mid-September review.

00:09:11 - Priya Nair: To recap next steps: Priya sends MSA/DPA redlines + clause cheat sheet; Ben uploads SOC2 summary, pen-test note, network diagram, and a tech packet with bench plan; Priya sends pricing worksheet. Customer to share vendor intake form and redline comments. Any corrections?
00:09:28 - Leah Morales: That is correct. I'll add my preferred clause language and circulate internally once I have the redline.
00:09:34 - Sam Patel: Sounds good. We'll expect docs by the dates we discussed. I'll coordinate PO approvers list once Leah confirms legal OK.
00:09:41 - Priya Nair: Fantastic — thanks everyone. We'll follow up by email with links and owners. We'll plan the technical deep-dive the week of Sep 8 if that works for you, Jordan.
00:09:50 - Jordan Wu: That works. Thanks Priya, Ben, Leah, Sam — talk soon.
00:09:55 - Priya Nair: Thanks all, bye.
